jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Radiopharmaceuticals - EMEA
jobs.description:
Senior Project Manager

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who has expertise within Radiopharmaceuticals ideally Radio Ligland Therapy ( RLT ) to join a team working within life changing precision cancer research. As a Senior Clinical Project Manager at ICON, you will be responsible for leading and managing cross functional projects, ensuring successful execution and delivery of project objectives, including those supporting radiopharmaceutical and radioligand-based clinical programs.

What You Will Do

You will manage day-to-day project and program management activities, supporting your team to deliver quality outcomes across EMEA working as a wider global team.

Key Responsibilities Include

Developing and executing clinical project plans, focusing on achieving project goals and objectives, including those for radiopharmaceutical and radioligand studies with specialized operational requirements.
Leading cross-functional teams to ensure the successful implementation of project activities.
Collaborating with stakeholders to identify project requirements and define project scope.
Mentoring and guiding team members, fostering a culture of excellence and continuous improvement.
Driving the development of project documentation and reports to present findings to stakeholders in a clear and actionable manner.
Staying abreast of industry trends and emerging technologies, including advancements in precision medicine, radiopharmaceuticals, and targeted oncology therapies, to integrate best practices into project management strategies.
Contributing to organizational growth through effective project leadership and strategic planning.

Your Profile

You will have solid clinical project and program management experience, with the ability to manage competing priorities and develop your team. Required qualifications and experience:

Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific discipline or healthcare-related field.
Experience in radiopharmaceuticals, or radioligand therapies is required.
Extensive experience in project management, with a proven track record of leading successful projects in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry
Strong proficiency in project management tools and methodologies, with excellent attention to detail.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop effective project strategies.
Demonstrated leadership skills, with experience in managing and mentoring teams effectively.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to convey technical concepts to diverse audiences.
Detail-oriented, with strong organizational skills to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a dynamic environment.
Willingness to travel as required (approximately 25%).

What ICON Can Offer You

Our success depends on the quality of our people. That’s why we’ve made it a priority to build a diverse culture that rewards high performance and nurtures talent.

In addition to your competitive salary, ICON offers a range of additional benefits. Our benefits are designed to be competitive within each country and are focused on well-being and work life balance opportunities for you and your family.

Our Benefits Examples Include

Various annual leave entitlements
A range of health insurance offerings to suit you and your family’s needs.
Competitive retirement planning offerings to maximize savings and plan with confidence for the years ahead.
Global Employee Assistance Programme, LifeWorks, offering 24-hour access to a global network of over 80,000 independent specialized professionals who are there to support you and your family’s well-being.
Life assurance
Flexible country-specific optional benefits, including childcare vouchers, bike purchase schemes, discounted gym memberships, subsidized travel passes, health assessments, among others.

Visit our careers site to read more about the benefits ICON offers.

At ICON, inclusion & belonging are fundamental to our culture and values. We’re dedicated to providing an inclusive and accessible environment for all candidates. ICON is committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, or in order to perform the essential functions of a position, please let us know or submit a request here

jobs.title: Senior Risk Program Manager - Fraud & Disputes Enablement
jobs.description:
About the Team:

Mercury* is building a complete financial stack for startups, and Risk is how we protect our customers, Mercury, and the broader financial ecosystem. You'll join the Fraud & Disputes Enablement team, a shared-services group that makes our operations teams faster, more consistent, and ready for scrutiny. The team is made up of Quality Control, Learning & Development, and Program Management, and supports Fraud & Disputes.

Role Summary:

This is a generalist program management role for someone who builds programs from zero to one. You'll lead Mercury's Bank Charter Readiness work across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX, run the operating reviews and goal tracking that show leaders how Fraud and Disputes are performing, and use data to drive continuous improvement. You'll work with Risk Operations, Compliance, Risk Product, Engineering, Risk Strategy, and Vendor Management, and you'll show the team how AI can help us work smarter, not harder.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What You'll Do:

Lead Bank Charter Readiness

Translate the regulatory expectations of a chartered bank (Reg E, card network rules, and the standards examiners apply) into clear, sequenced work plans owned by the right teams.
Build Bank Charter Readiness programs from zero to one: define scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks, and report progress to executives.
Keep teams audit-ready every day, with current SOPs, traceable decisions, defensible evidence, and clean documentation, so exam preparation never becomes a scramble.
Coordinate responses to regulator, auditor, and partner-bank inquiries with Compliance, Legal, and Operations.

Lead Goal tracking, and Reporting for Fraud & Disputes

Own the cadence and content of Operational Quality Reviews and Monthly CORs Reviews for Fraud and Disputes, from the data pull to the narrative to the follow-up actions.
Define and track ops health measures and team goals, including OKRs, so leaders can see what is on track, what is at risk, and why.
Build the reporting and dashboards leaders use to make decisions, and set up new reporting from scratch where none exists.
Raise risks early, make trade-offs explicit, and drive decisions to closure with partners who don't report to you.

Use data for continuous improvement

Analyze quality, productivity, and compliance data across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX to find the patterns behind recurring problems.
Turn those findings into durable process, tooling, and reporting improvements instead of one-off fixes.
Work with QC, L&D, and Operations leaders to route root causes to the team that can fix them, and confirm the fix worked.
Stand up new continuous improvement programs from zero to one and measure their results.

What You'll Bring:

5+ years of program management experience in risk, compliance, fraud, disputes, or operations at a bank, fintech, or other regulated financial services company.
Banking* experience, with working knowledge of how a regulated institution runs, and direct experience working with regulators, examiners, auditors, or sponsor banks (for example exam preparation, findings remediation, or regulatory responses).
A record of building programs from zero to one, from ambiguous problem to measurable result, with impact beyond your immediate team.
2+ years of experience governing BPO or other outsourced operations, with a focus on governance: SLAs, performance and quality oversight, escalations, and regular business reviews.
Strong understanding of risk operational processes in Fraud and/or Disputes, such as case handling, investigations, chargebacks, or Reg E error resolution.
Comfort with data: you can define metrics, build or interpret dashboards, and explain what the numbers mean.
Experience using AI and automation to improve how work gets done, for example synthesizing evidence and documentation, drafting and maintaining SOPs, analyzing QC and vendor data, summarizing incidents, and automating status reporting.

Nice to Haves:

Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or above) or equivalent continuous improvement experience
ISO quality credentials (for example ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Implementer) or a similar quality management background
PMI certification (PMP, PgMP) or equivalent
Experience with change management frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR, or ITIL-style incident and problem management
Experience in QC program design, workforce management, or learning and development
Familiarity with card network dispute rules and platforms
Experience with Risk UX, customer-facing risk flows, in a regulated context
Experience building and scaling a program in a high-growth environment

Change Enablement and Readiness

jobs.title: MOI Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Administers all finance, human resources and facilities and other operational activities for small to mid-sized academic or research program. Administers major program components, and some or all of the program's operational requirements. Develops and organizes conferences and other public forums. Works under direction of Principal Investigator or more senior Academic Program Officer to establish center agenda, funding, objectives.

The Molecular Oncology Initiative (MOI) at UCSF is responsible for enabling precision oncology for cancer patients at UCSF, driving both the clinical implementation of personalized cancer care and the research that advances it.

MOI provides support for clinicians in the interpretation of our own internal tumor sequencing platform (UCSF500) as well as platforms offered by external vendors.

The MOI Program Manager will play a central role in this mission, operating under the direction of the MOI Director and Associate Director as well as supervision by HDFCCC administration.

The MOI Program Manager will lead the MOI Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC), reviewing and quality controlling the work and providing constructive, actionable feedback to support accuracy and continuous improvement in data collection and abstraction activities.

The MOI Program Manager will be expected to work with considerable independence alongside MOI team members to execute MOI activities, taking ownership of implementation while operating within a framework of regular oversight and guidance .

The current job responsibilities for this position do not involve any direct patient contact. Candidates must live or plan to move to the Bay Area and are required to come to Mission Bay campus at least twice and preferably three times a week.

This Position Has Two Core Areas Of Responsibility

Program Management — serving as the operational backbone for MOI's clinical and research activities, shepherding projects from inception to completion
Data Quality Management — taking a leading role in designing, testing, and implementing automated pipelines for the collection and quality assurance of clinical and genomic data across all MOI projects, while also performing manual QC as required to ensure data integrity across all activities.This includes also design and data management using RedCap and other database tools.

Department Overview

The UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center (HDFCCC) is redefining what is possible by advancing cancer research and patient care. By unifying outstanding researchers and clinicians, the center minimizes cancer incidence, establishes new frontiers in cancer care, and improves our patients’ lives. We have received the prestigious designation of “comprehensive” from the National Cancer Institute (NCI).We combine basic science, clinical research, epidemiology, cancer control and patient care throughout the University of California, San Francisco.

The Molecular Oncology Initiative (MOI) at UCSF is responsible for enabling precision oncology for cancer patients at UCSF, driving both the clinical implementation of personalized cancer care and the research that advances it. MOI provides support for clinicians in the interpretation of our own internal tumor sequencing platform (UCSF500) as well as platforms offered by external vendors.

Qualifications

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training required including but not limited to biological sciences, biomedical informatics, public health, or a related discipline.
Minimum of 3 years of experience in program management, data quality control, or a related role, preferably in an academic medical or research setting
Strong foundational knowledge of medical terminology and clinical oncology concepts, including cancer diagnoses, staging, pathology, imaging, and treatment modalities (e.g. surgical, systemic, and radiation therapies); this knowledge is essential for independently and accurately performing quality control of clinical oncology data abstractions
Demonstrated experience with IRB submissions, contract management, or other research compliance and oversight activities
Experience performing clinical data abstraction and/or quality control of clinical or genomic data
Familiarity with electronic health records (EHR) and the ability to navigate complex patient clinical histories spanning diagnoses, imaging, pathology, and treatment records
Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, maintain document control systems, and track and follow up on action items across a team to ensure project/task completion in a timely manner.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear meeting notes, program updates, and reports for diverse audiences
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively, with a demonstrated capacity to proactively identify problems and develop solutions with minimal supervision
Proficiency with standard project management tools.
Prior experience with various computer programs (Microsoft Office; internet-based databases).
Ability to sit and work at a computer for several hours per day. May need to travel between one or more campuses via UCSF shuttle.
Ability to work with a sensitive population of patients (oncology patients).
Ability to work well independently, complete projects in a timely manner, and prioritize multiple projects to ensure the completion of essential tasks by deadlines.
Excellent problem-solving skills and able to use good judgement in application of problem-solving skills.
Effective at applying constructive feedback on projects and performance.
Thorough knowledge of administrative, budgetary, human resources and financial principles and practices.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Strong ability to think creatively and independently on concepts requiring advanced analytical skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work with diverse groups to achieve results.
Strong ability to work collaboratively with internal and external peers and managers.

Preferred

Terminal degree in a related area (PhD, JD, MD, etc.) such as biological sciences, biomedical informatics, computational biology, public health, or oncology-related discipline and / or equivalent experience / training.
3–4 years of experience in program management and/or data quality control, ideally within a precision medicine, oncology, or genomics program
Familiarity with cancer genomics and next-generation sequencing (NGS), including experience interpreting or working with NGS test results such as the UCSF500 panel
Experience with oncology-specific data standards and ontologies, including OncoTree or similar cancer classification systems
Experience with REDCap database design, build, and maintenance
Experience designing or implementing automated data abstraction or QC pipelines
Practical experience working with large language models (LLMs) and the ability to thoughtfully evaluate when LLM-based solutions are appropriate versus rule-based or heuristic approaches
Experience providing feedback, guidance, or informal mentorship to junior research staff or coordinators
Familiarity with UCSF systems and institutional policies, including UCSF research compliance frameworks
Solid fundraising experience.
Academic background and experience in selected area of research preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training required including but not limited to biological sciences, biomedical informatics, public health, or a related discipline.

About Us

About UCSF

The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is a leading university dedicated to promoting health worldwide through advanced biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care. It is the only campus in the 10-campus UC system dedicated exclusively to the health sciences. We bring together the world’s leading experts in nearly every area of health. We are home to five Nobel laureates who have advanced the understanding of cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, aging and stem cells.

Pride Values

UCSF is a diverse community made of people with many skills and talents. We seek candidates whose work experience or community service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to professionalism, respect, integrity, diversity and excellence – also known as our PRIDE values .

In addition to our PRIDE values, UCSF is committed to equity – both in how we deliver care as well as our workforce. We are committed to building a broadly diverse community, nurturing a culture that is welcoming and supportive, and engaging diverse ideas for the provision of culturally competent education, discovery, and patient care. Additional information about UCSF is available here .

Join us to find a rewarding career contributing to improving healthcare worldwide.

You'll lead Mercury's Bank Charter Readiness work across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX, run the operating reviews and goal tracking that show leaders how Fraud and Disputes are performing, and use data to drive continuous improvement. As Embedded SW TPM, you will be the connective tissue between silicon, platforms and systems

teams, driving the embedded and low-level software programs that enable EN100 (and future

accelerators) to run real AI workloads reliably and efficiently. You'll own the program plan from

architecture through bring-up, pre-/post- silicon validation, and customer/OEM deployment to

surface risks before they become blockers and keeping a hardware-coupled software org moving

in lockstep with silicon milestones.

What You'll Do

Own end-to-end program management for embedded software workstreams: device

drivers, firmware, boot-loaders and board support packages for EnCharge accelerators.

Build and maintain integrated program schedules that align embedded software milestones

with chip tape-out, silicon bring-up, board bring-up, and customer/OEM delivery dates.

Partner closely with embedded software, ASIC/hardware, platform and validation teams to

define scope, sequence dependencies, and track execution against plan.

Identify, track, and drive resolution of cross-team risks and blockers (e.g., silicon errata

affecting driver behavior, toolchain dependencies, host OS/driver compatibility).

Drive silicon bring-up and platform enablement, including early firmware, boot flows,

device initialization, memory management, command submission, interrupts, power

management, and hardware/software integration.

Run the program's operating cadence: planning, standups, milestone reviews,

ceremony.

Drive execution across geographically distributed engineering teams and external partners

as needed.

Help build the program management function like process, tooling, and reporting.

What We're Looking For

8+ years of technical program or project management experience, with a meaningful

portion spent on embedded software, drivers, firmware, or low-level systems software.

Direct experience coordinating software programs tightly coupled to hardware (silicon

bring-up, board bring-up, or similar), ideally in AI/ML accelerators, semiconductors,

robotics, or a related hardware-software domain.

Background in Linux kernel driver development processes, JTAG/lab-based debug

workflows, or hardware validation methodologies.

Experience with FPGA simulation and emulator environments like Zebu, Veloce,

Palladium.

Strong understanding of areas such as:
Embedded firmware
Device drivers
SoC/accelerator architecture
Memory and DMA
Interrupts and command queues
Boot and initialization
Hardware/software interfaces
Performance and system-level debugging
Track record of managing complex, multi-team schedules with hard external dependencies

(tape-out dates, partner deliverables, customer commitments) and keeping them honest.

Strong risk management instincts — you find the thing that's going to break the schedule

two months before it does.

Excellent written and verbal communication; able to flex between engineering detail and

Experience with AI accelerators, GPUs, NPUs, DSPs, or other heterogeneous compute

architectures.

Experience with silicon bring-up and early hardware/software co-development.
Experience with firmware for custom accelerators or SoCs.
Experience working across firmware, driver, compiler, and runtime teams.
Experience with simulation/emulation environments used for pre-silicon software

development.

Experience with Linux kernel, embedded Linux, RTOS, or low-level systems software.
Experience managing external engineering partners or vendors.

Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

U.S. Bank’s Digital Assets and Emerging Money Movement team is seeking an effective Senior Program/Project Manager
with demonstrated program leadership and project management experience to contribute to the success of our enterprise money movement initiatives. This role sits within a new and evolving team focused on enterprise‑level money movement strategy.

This individual will lead and direct large, complex programs in support of the bank’s overall money movement strategy. The role provides direction to project staff across multiple workstreams and stages within assigned programs, establishes program governance, and drives execution to ensure initiatives are implemented, adopted, and operating effectively. The Senior Program/Project Manager translates corporate objectives into clear program objectives, operating practices, and measurable outcomes.

The Emerging Money Movement team operates with an enterprise‑first mandate
and is not aligned to a single business line. While individual business lines retain ownership of their own product roadmaps and growth strategies, this team focuses on cross‑line‑of‑business coordination, optimization, and reuse of money movement capabilities to reduce duplication and drive enterprise‑wide efficiency.

The team is evolving from a historical focus on external advocacy and industry engagement toward a model centered on internal enterprise program leadership and strategic coordination. This role operates within a heavy partnership model, working closely with product leaders across business lines, platform, operations, and technology teams, as well as legal, risk, compliance, and advocacy partners. The role also interfaces externally with payment networks and industry partners, including Visa, Mastercard, and other payment system operators.

Due to the enterprise scope of this work, there will be intentional organizational friction, requiring strong alignment, influence, and leadership across teams without direct authority. The successful candidate will balance strategic leadership with disciplined execution, shaping direction, priorities, and investment decisions while driving delivery of emerging and traditional money movement capabilities at scale.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience
At least 10 years experience with tools and techniques for planning, organizing, monitoring and controlling IT projects.

Preferred Qualifications:

Significant experience leading large, complex, cross‑functional programs within a financial services or payments environment

jobs.title: Program Manager, Inventory Strategy and Ops
jobs.description:
At Compass, our mission is to help everyone find their place in the world. Founded in 2012, we’re revolutionizing the real estate industry with our end-to-end platform that empowers residential real estate agents to deliver exceptional service to seller and buyer clients.

Compass International Holdings is seeking a Program Manager of Inventory Strategy & Enablement to own the national programs that increase inventory on the platform. This role exists for one reason: agents across our ten brands should win more listing agreements, launch them through our technology platform, and do it as a matter of habit rather than a one-time campaign.

You will own the full arc, from identifying where the opportunity is, to designing the program, to piloting it in a brand and/or region, to rolling it out across every brand and making it stick. You will also own the creation and distribution of what the field actually receives: the playbooks, the talk tracks, the training, and the follow-through that turn a strategy into agent behavior.

This is a builder and operator role. You will learn from what has already worked, bring structure and rigor to scale it, and hold yourself accountable to a number. If you are energized by turning ideas into programs that move measurable inventory, this is the seat.

What You'll Own

Inventory Adoption & Portfolio Strategy

Contribute to and deliver the national strategy for driving inventory onto the platform across agent segments and brands, grounded in field research and discovery, not assumption
Design programs that create behavior change and habit formation, so agents consistently win listing agreements and launch them through Compass technology
Translate product capability into adoption strategy that resonates with the field, framed in agent and client value rather than feature language, across each brand
Manage project scopes, charters, and risk mitigation strategies across high-priority inventory growth workstreams
Identify where the biggest inventory unlocks sit, by brand, by region, by segment, and go after them in priority order

Program Build and National Scale

Own the end-to-end project lifecycle of adoption initiatives, defining key milestones, deliverables, resource allocation, and timelines from ideation to national rollout
Build standardized project management frameworks, governance models, playbooks, and systems to scale program delivery without linear headcount
Run the readiness path end-to-end for every initiative: workback schedule built and approved by the regions and Legal, assets created for each brand plus a generic version, and employees, agents, and staff trained before launch
Keep programs aligned to the business priorities they serve: inventory growth, agent productivity, and retention
Establish robust risk management and issue tracking protocols to proactively resolve project bottlenecks and dependency conflicts

Field Enablement and Standardization

Own the design and launch of the enablement and training that carry each program into the field, including brand-adaptable decks, talk tracks, and seller-facing collateral
Build frameworks that create consistency and standardization across regions and brands, while leaving room for each brand's voice
Partner with Academy, Coaching, and brand learning teams on development and rollout, and hold the accountability for whether the field is genuinely equipped
Identify operational gaps in how regional teams execute and implement scalable fixes

Cross-Functional Alignment

Build trusted relationships with stakeholders at every level, from agents and regional staff to brand leadership
Partner with Product to align adoption strategy with the feature roadmap and release cycles
Work with Marketing, Product Marketing, and Communications to position tools around agent and client value
Serve as the connective tissue between regional teams and central functions, and translate field feedback into actionable insight for partner teams
Embed adoption into daily workflows and conversations with Brand Leadership, Regional Presidents, Sales Leadership, and Coaching

Performance and Insight

Define success metrics for every initiative and own the reporting against them
Use dashboards and field insight together to refine programs in flight, since neither alone tells you why something is or is not working
Surface patterns, gaps, and acceleration opportunities to leadership with a recommendation attached, not just a readout
Prepare executive-ready updates and materials that drive decisions, not just status

Influence

Act as a strategic thought partner to brand and regional leadership on inventory priorities
Influence without authority across a highly matrixed, multi-brand organization, and drive alignment and execution anyway

What You Bring

5+ years in program management, strategy, operations, GTM, or enablement in a technology-driven environment
A track record of building and scaling programs that produced measurable behavior change, with the numbers to show it
Proven mastery of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, or Hybrid), project tracking tools, and workback schedule execution
PMP, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project management certification is a strong plus
Data-driven mindset, comfortable defining metrics, building the tracking, and changing course when the data says so
Strong writer and presenter who can turn complex strategy into clear, field-ready materials and executive communications
Exceptional cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management, especially with senior leaders who do not report to you
Highly organized, strong attention to detail, and dependable follow-through on long-running initiatives
Comfortable navigating ambiguity, change, and shifting priorities across many concurrent workstreams
Positive, solutions-oriented, self-starting, and able to execute independently
Experience in real estate brokerage, SaaS, or multi-brand organizations is a strong plus
Working knowledge of brokerage operations and the Agent Experience function is a plus

Why This Role Matters

Inventory is the engine of the business. This role is how Compass technology turns into listings on the platform, consistently, across every brand, at national scale. You will be responsible for turning innovation into action, and action into inventory.

Compensation

The base pay range for this position is $142,200-$158,000 annually; however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Bonuses and restricted stock units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to a full range of benefits. Base pay is based on market location. Minimum wage for the position will always be met.

Perks That You Need To Know About

Participation in our incentive programs (which may include eligible cash, equity, or commissions). Plus paid vacation, holidays, sick time, parental leave, and recharge leave; medical, tele-health, dental and vision benefits; 401(k) plan; flexible spending accounts (FSAs); commuter program; life and disability insurance; Maven (a support system for new parents); Carrot (fertility benefits); UrbanSitter (caregiver referral network); Employee Assistance Program; and pet insurance.

Do your best work, be your authentic self.
At Compass, we believe that everyone deserves to find their place in the world — a place where they feel like they belong, where they can be their authentic selves, where they can thrive. Our collaborative, energetic culture is grounded in our Compass Entrepreneurship Principles and our commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, growth and mobility. As an equal opportunity employer, we offer competitive compensation packages, robust benefits and professional growth opportunities aimed at helping to improve our employees' lives and careers.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Project Manager II
to oversee complex international clinical programs supporting infectious diseases. This clinical project management position will engage across a large contingency of stakeholders and multiple sites with responsibility to ensure timely execution of milestones for the entire lifecycle of the assignments.

This position will be in support of the Global-Infectious Diseases portfolio.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Serve as project lead for assigned studies, managing all timelines, deliverables, and fiscal responsibilities.
Serve as primary point of contact with stakeholders including PI, Research Physicians, Project Sponsor including Military leadership, Clinical Operations, Data Coordinating Center and Product Quality groups, as examples.
Responsible for operational management of clinical research by applying comprehensive knowledge of clinical development and project management to help lead and develop appropriate project plans, work with the project team to refine plans and establish realistic targets for task completion, develop and implement communications plans, and monitor progress throughout the life of the study.
Coordinate operational, administrative and diverse programmatic activities for the Clinical Research Directorate project teams for international clinical studies. Project teams may include research physicians, statisticians, pharmacists, data managers, regulatory specialists, site PI and study teams, clinical and research laboratory experts, research collaborators, human resources, budget analysts, and contracting.
Coordinate communications within project team, organizing meetings and developing appropriate agendas, coordinating meeting minutes and their appropriate dissemination, following up on action items with responsible parties.
Assess risks to project performance, and independently or in collaboration with study team, develop risk mitigation proposals for consideration by responsible leadership. Implement selected mitigation plans and monitor outcomes.
Develop, track and manage project budgets, prepare statements of work and budget justifications for contract requisitions.
Serve as the primary liaison with finance and grants management teams for forecasting, financial planning, budget execution, and reporting activities.
Review financial reports, monitor expenditures, provide financial analyses and recommendations to leadership and Principal Investigators to support effective financial management and resource allocation.
Manage the process for collaboration agreements and liaise with Technology Transfer and Office of Sponsored Programs. Support and participate in planning, creation and submission of proposals and agreements (CRADA, MTA, NDA, Data Use agreements as examples). Other related professional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor's Degree in a science related field; Master's Degree preferred.
Minimum of 3-5 years experience required.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to work in a fast-paced research environment, and to plan and manage multiple priorities on different timelines.
Experience managing multicenter clinical research studies, international collaborations, or global health programs preferred.
Ability to incorporate strategic vision of leadership into plans and operations with attention to detail leading to optimized cost, time and performance outcomes. Ability to manage complex issues with multiple partners and stakeholders. Flexibility to handle a variety of tasks and shift priorities as necessary.
Excellent organization, time and project management skills with strong interpersonal skills. Ability to effectively interact with local and international external collaborators in a culturally sensitive manner.
Ability to work as an effective team member in a virtual environment. High level of initiative and ability to work with minimal supervision.
Ability to clearly communicate verbally and in writing, build and maintain teams, and identify and resolve problems.
Knowledge of federal budget processes and fundamental principles of project management.
Working knowledge of clinical research regulatory processes. Proficiency in standard project management software and budgeting tools, including but not limited to; Smartsheet, REDCap and Oracle and/or other web-based software systems.
Experience working within a DoD funded agreement a plus.
Experience with International clinical trials including vaccines, therapeutics and/or cohort studies for infectious disease indications preferred.

Work Environment

This position is hybrid and may take place primarily in an office setting.

Compensation

The annual salary range for this position is $67,500-$90,000. Actual salary will be determined based on experience, education, etc.

Benefits

HJF offers a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on your health and well-being, from medical, dental, and vision coverage to health savings and retirement plans, and more.

Employment with HJF is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, which may include, but is not limited to, contacting your professional references, verification of previous employment, education and credentials, a criminal background check, and a department of motor vehicle (DMV) check if applicable. Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Department Overview

Silvus Technologies is dedicated to one mission: connecting those who keep us safe. We do so by delivering the most advanced Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET) radios powered by our custom and ever evolving Mobile-Networked MIMO waveform. Together, our radios and waveform provide vital communications for mission critical applications in the harshest environments from underground tunnels to high altitude balloons.

Silvus StreamCaster™ radios are being rapidly adopted by customers all over the world ranging from the U.S. and Allied Nations Departments of Defense, to International, Federal, State and Local Law Enforcement agencies, all the way to the Superbowl, Grammys and industry-leading drone, robot, and unmanned systems manufacturers.

Would you like to join an incredibly talented group of people, doing very challenging work, with the prime directive of “Keeping Our Heroes Connected”?

Job Description

THE OPPORTUNITY

Silvus Technologies, the global leader in advanced MIMO mesh networking solutions for defense, industrial, and public safety applications, is seeking an R&D Technical Program Manager
reporting to the Vice President of Research and Development. The successful individual in this role will drive execution excellence across our next-generation products.

You’ll partner closely with senior R&D and engineering leadership, and all functional and product teams to define best practices, drive cross-functional execution, and deliver high-impact products to our customers.

You will be part of a passionate team redefining RF sensing, electronic warfare and wireless connectivity in the most demanding environments, from battlefield networks and autonomous systems to public safety and industrial applications. You will work alongside world-class engineers solving real-world challenges, with opportunities to grow, innovate, and lead as our organization scales.

If you’re ready to help shape the future of communications and electronic warfare and establish the foundation of Silvus’ Program Management organization, we’d love to meet you.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Project Manager - Large Load & Interconnection
to support the rapid growth of data centers, AI infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, battery storage, and other large-load developments across North America.

This role combines client advisory, business development, technical due diligence, and hands-on project execution. The successful candidate will help clients navigate complex utility and transmission interconnection challenges — from early-stage site selection and power availability due diligence through utility engagement, interconnection studies, infrastructure planning, and project delivery — while building and leading a multidisciplinary team.

Working closely with developers, hyperscalers, utilities, independent power producers, and investors, this individual will serve as a trusted day-to-day technical leader throughout the project lifecycle. This is a role for someone who takes initiative without needing to be asked, is comfortable doing whatever the project actually needs — from a client pitch to a model run — reads clients and colleagues well enough to know when to lead and when to defer, and is motivated as much by building a strong team underneath them as by their own advancement.

What You'll Do

Client Engagement & Market Development
Develop and maintain relationships with data center developers, hyperscalers, utilities, transmission owners, renewable developers, and large industrial customers.
Identify and pursue opportunities related to grid interconnections, utility service strategy, transmission planning, and power infrastructure development.
Own proposal development, scope definition, fee development, and client presentations.
Represent AECOM at industry conferences, client workshops, and business development events, and bring back what's learned to sharpen the team's approach.
Help grow AECOM's Power Interconnection practice through exceptional client service, successful project delivery, and a genuine hand in building out the team and its capabilities.

Project Management & Execution
Manage multiple interconnection, due diligence, and power advisory projects simultaneously.
Lead project planning, scheduling, budgeting, resource management, and client communications.
Coordinate multidisciplinary project teams including transmission planners, electrical engineers, civil engineers, environmental specialists, and permitting professionals.
Monitor project risks and develop mitigation strategies to maintain schedule and budget objectives.
Deliver high-quality reports, presentations, and client recommendations, and stay close enough to the work to catch problems before the client does.

Technical Due Diligence & Siting Investigation
Lead technical due diligence for data center and large-load site selection, evaluating power infrastructure availability, utility readiness, and transmission system accessibility.
Direct siting investigations that weigh grid access, interconnection timelines, and infrastructure constraints alongside a site's broader technical and commercial viability.
Advise clients on utility constraints, transmission availability, interconnection queues, network upgrades, reliability considerations, and development risks — early enough to shape a site decision, not just react to one.
Guide clients through utility coordination, interconnection processes, and regulatory requirements across North American markets.
Develop power strategies that align infrastructure development schedules with grid availability and project objectives.

Qualifications

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:
BA/BS in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems or related field + 6 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Proven experience supporting utility, data center, renewable energy, generation, transmission, or large-load projects
Proven experience managing technical projects and interacting directly with clients
Demonstrated experience supporting data center, AI infrastructure, semiconductor, or advanced manufacturing projects
6 years of project management experience
Demonstrated experience in transmission planning, interconnection services, utility planning, power system consulting, or energy infrastructure development
This position requires travel as needed

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Masters Degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems or related field
Professional Engineer (PE) license
10+ years of progressive experience in transmission planning, interconnection services, or power system consulting, with a track record of winning and leading client work
Previous management of power systems, utility infrastructure, and transmission planning principles
Knowledge of PJM, ERCOT, MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, and regulated utility environments
Experience and proven success in client relationships and business development
Experience leading technical due diligence or siting investigations tied to power availability
Experience with utility service studies, load interconnections, generator interconnections, and transmission planning studies
Familiarity with NERC, FERC, ISO, and RTO requirements
Experience using PSS®E, PSLF, PowerWorld, PSCAD, ETAP, EMTP/ATP, Promod, or similar tools.
Prior experience building or growing a technical team or practice area, and a genuine appetite for doing it again here

Additional Information

Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
Relocation is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $110000 to $140000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Manager
jobs.description:
Why Work at Banner?

For over 50 years, Banner Engineering has been at the forefront of industrial automation. We offer products and solutions including award-winning sensors, wireless solutions, machine safety, indication and LED lighting. From Fortune 500 leaders to innovative startups, Banner's award-winning products and solutions are helping companies around the world increase efficiency, reduce costs, safeguard equipment, and protect personnel. Our commitment to innovation shows through a continuous, market-driven evolution of products and technology. With engineers employed in nearly every major department, engineering is in our DNA.

Banner is a rapidly growing company that offers many personal development opportunities, an excellent benefits package, and a collaborative team of employees who are passionate about what they do.

Position Summary

The Cybersecurity Manager leads the organization’s cybersecurity program, protecting Banner’s information, technology, operations, and digital assets from evolving threats. This role is responsible for defining and operating security governance, risk management, security operations, vulnerability management, incident response, and security awareness across the global enterprise. Partnering with IT/OT leaders, business teams, and third parties the Cybersecurity Manager translates business needs and risk into practical, scalable security controls that enable Banner’s continued growth.

This position reports to the VP of IT/OT.

What You’ll Be Doing

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working both individually and collaboratively, staying on top of tasks, and making a meaningful impact across teams and projects. Below are some key responsibilities of the role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and continuously improve Banner’s global cybersecurity program, aligning security strategy, priorities, and investments with business objectives and risk.
Develop, maintain, and enforce cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, and governance practices consistent with recognized frameworks and applicable requirements.
Direct security operations, including threat monitoring, security event triage, investigations, incident response, and coordination with internal and external partners.
Manage the vulnerability-management program, including vulnerability identification, risk-based prioritization, remediation tracking, validation, and executive escalation.
Lead cybersecurity risk assessments for enterprise systems, cloud services, manufacturing and operational technology environments, vendors, and new technology initiatives.
Partner with Infrastructure, Applications, Engineering, Manufacturing, Legal, HR, and business leaders to embed appropriate security requirements into projects, processes, and services.
Oversee cybersecurity vendor relationships, managed security services, contracts, and service-level expectations to ensure effective and cost-conscious protection.
Develop and report meaningful cybersecurity metrics, risk trends, and program status to IT/OT leadership and executive stakeholders.
Lead, coach, and develop cybersecurity personnel and foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and shared responsibility for security.

What You Bring To The Table

To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily, and regular attendance is required. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to support individuals with disabilities.

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field
7+ years of progressive cybersecurity or information-security experience, including leadership or program-management responsibility.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise cybersecurity programs, security operations, and risk-based improvement initiatives.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity principles, security controls, and frameworks such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, and CIS Controls.
Experience with incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access management, security monitoring, and third-party risk management.
Experience securing a hybrid on-premises and cloud technology environment, including on-premises infrastructure, cloud platforms and services, endpoints, networks, and operational technology or industrial environments.
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to explain risk and recommendations clearly to technical and business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing risks, build practical security roadmaps, and drive cross-functional execution.

Preferred

Master’s degree preferred
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GIAC, CCSP, or equivalent preferred.
Experience working in a fast-paced environment
Experience working for an Industrial Manufacturing company

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has direct supervisory responsibilities for cybersecurity personnel and is responsible for hiring, training, evaluating performance, managing workloads, and addressing disciplinary issues in accordance with company policies.

Job Description

The Senior Security Project Manager
leads complex SCIF/SAPF and secure-facility projects from planning and design through construction, testing, accreditation, and closeout. The role integrates project management, security requirements, construction, accreditation, TEMPEST coordination, and customer engagement to ensure successful project delivery.

The Sr. Security Project Manager works directly with government customers, AOs, security authorities, SSOs, PSOs, CPSOs, designers, contractors, and technical SMEs to identify risks, resolve issues, and ensure security requirements are effectively incorporated into project execution.

The position requires substantial experience in secure-facility construction and security management, with strong knowledge of ICD 705 and applicable security requirements. The Sr. Security Project Manager is responsible for accreditation readiness and documentation, project-level TEMPEST coordination, and managing the associated impacts to scope, schedule, cost, risk, and construction.

Extensive SCIF/SAPF construction site experience is required. Experience serving as an SSM or in an equivalent security-management role is strongly preferred.

This is a hybrid role with the primary worksite located near Denver, CO. Candidates in all locations will be considered, but travel will be required
for the role.

Primary Responsibilities

Independently manage complex, high-priority, and strategically important SCIF/SAPF and secure-facility projects.
Maintain accountability for project scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, customer satisfaction, security requirements, and accreditation outcomes.
Develop and maintain integrated project execution plans connecting security requirements, design, procurement, construction, testing, accreditation, and closeout activities.
Lead project-level security-management coordination with Security Consultants, security SMEs, customer security stakeholders, and government personnel.
Apply practical and comprehensive knowledge of ICD 705 and applicable Department of War (DoW), Intelligence Community (IC), and other applicable security requirements.
Lead security requirements through all phases of the project lifecycle, including planning, design, construction, testing and verification, accreditation, and closeout.
Lead accreditation-package development and readiness, including document completeness, internal reviews, customer and AO comments, corrective actions, revisions, and submission milestones.
Work directly with AOs, security authorities, government security personnel, customers, designers, contractors, construction teams, and technical SMEs to resolve security and accreditation issues.
Lead project-level TEMPEST coordination and manage associated impacts to design, construction, documentation, testing, schedule, cost, and risk.
Identify when security or TEMPEST matters require specialized technical escalation and ensure decisions, assumptions, mitigation measures, and resolutions are appropriately documented.
Proactively identify and manage security, accreditation, construction, schedule, cost, and technical risks before they adversely affect project execution or accreditation.
Lead complex customer, security, construction, and project meetings and communicate project requirements, decisions, risks, status, and action items clearly and professionally.
Provide senior-level field leadership during SCIF/SAPF construction activities and coordinate the resolution of security-related site issues.
Review project deliverables and documentation for completeness, accuracy, compliance, and readiness for customer and accreditation review.
Coordinate with project managers, construction personnel, security professionals, designers, and technical SMEs to ensure security requirements are incorporated into project execution.
Mentor Project Managers and Junior Project Managers in project management, security management, accreditation, AO coordination, TEMPEST, customer engagement, and field execution.
Support Program Managers with complex customer, security, accreditation, AO, construction, and technical matters.
Lead or participate in cross-functional Tiger Teams and develop evidence-based recommendations for complex project or security issues.
Contribute to PMO standards, processes, lessons learned, security-management practices, templates, tools, and reusable methodologies.
Identify opportunities to improve project execution, security compliance, accreditation readiness, and customer satisfaction.
Support proposals, capture activities, pricing development, solution development, technical approaches, and other business-development activities.
Maintain professional relationships with government customers, industry partners, contractors, security authorities, and other project stakeholders.
Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications & Requirements

A bachelor's degree in construction management, project management, engineering, security management, business administration, or a related discipline is preferred. Equivalent education, training, certifications, and professional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
Minimum 7–10 years of experience in physical and technical security with expertise in NISPOM, ICD 705, SAPF requirements, and other applicable national security policies.
Extensive knowledge of TEMPEST, RF Shielding, RF and Acoustic Testing, Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM), Protected Distribution Systems (PDS), CNSSI 7003, and UL 2050 standards.
Substantial progressive experience in secure-facility construction, SCIF/SAPF project management, security management, accreditation, or a closely related field is required. Senior-level experience independently managing complex secure-facility projects is strongly preferred. Strong analytical, project management, and communication skills with the ability to advise clients and internal teams on technical security matters.
Ability to obtain and maintain the required U.S. Government security clearance.
This position requires travel to support projects and customer engagements across the United States. Travel may include extended or long-term assignments at project locations, potentially requiring several weeks or months away from the employee’s primary work location, based on project needs and business requirements.

Ability to sit, stand, walk, climb ladders, and lift up to 25 pounds in office and construction environments.

The individual will also provide continuity of program leadership and may perform CPM responsibilities when delegated by the Contractor Program Manager.

This is a hybrid position requiring some on-site presence.

Support the Contractor Program Manager in overseeing contract and subcontractor performance across all program locations and functional areas.
Coordinate regularly with Government program managers, the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), task leads, corporate leadership, and subcontractor representatives.
Prepare and consolidate financial, staffing, performance, risk, and program status information for recurring reports, reviews, and Government meetings.
Monitor contract expenditures, labor utilization, funding, burn rates, cost variances, and Estimated Cost at Completion (EAC) projections.

Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of the Program Management Plan (PMP), Quality Control Plan (QCP), transition plans, staffing plans, risk register, and associated management procedures.

Experience supporting the management of Federal Government contracts, including program execution, financial oversight, staffing, reporting, and contract deliverables.

Experience coordinating a geographically dispersed workforce consisting of employees, subcontractors, functional leads, and multiple Government stakeholders.
Experience supporting or implementing Program Management Plans, Quality Control Plans, transition plans, risk-management processes, and corrective-action procedures.
Experience managing staffing activities, including recruiting, onboarding, personnel tracking, vacancy management, retention, and performance monitoring.
Ability to organize and manage multiple concurrent deadlines, deliverables, meetings, and action items in a complex contract environment.
Proven ability to identify performance risks, develop practical mitigation strategies, and follow issues through resolution.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with Government program managers, CORs, contracting personnel, corporate leadership, employees, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Adobe Acrobat for preparing reports, presentations, spreadsheets, and contract documentation.

Experience supporting programs within NGA, the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, or another Federal Government organization.
Experience serving as a Deputy Program Manager, Operations Manager, Contract Manager, or senior program-management analyst on a contract of similar size, scope, and complexity.

Experience using Unanet or a comparable enterprise resource planning, contract accounting, or workforce-management system.

Master's degree in a business-related field and five (5) years of program or contract-management experience, or a bachelor's degree in a business-related field and seven (7) years of program or contract-management experience.

jobs.title: Senior Risk Program Manager - Fraud & Disputes Enablement
jobs.description:
About the Team:

Mercury* is building a complete financial stack for startups, and Risk is how we protect our customers, Mercury, and the broader financial ecosystem. You'll join the Fraud & Disputes Enablement team, a shared-services group that makes our operations teams faster, more consistent, and ready for scrutiny. The team is made up of Quality Control, Learning & Development, and Program Management, and supports Fraud & Disputes.

Role Summary:

This is a generalist program management role for someone who builds programs from zero to one. You'll lead Mercury's Bank Charter Readiness work across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX, run the operating reviews and goal tracking that show leaders how Fraud and Disputes are performing, and use data to drive continuous improvement. You'll work with Risk Operations, Compliance, Risk Product, Engineering, Risk Strategy, and Vendor Management, and you'll show the team how AI can help us work smarter, not harder.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What You'll Do:

Lead Bank Charter Readiness

Translate the regulatory expectations of a chartered bank (Reg E, card network rules, and the standards examiners apply) into clear, sequenced work plans owned by the right teams.
Build Bank Charter Readiness programs from zero to one: define scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks, and report progress to executives.
Keep teams audit-ready every day, with current SOPs, traceable decisions, defensible evidence, and clean documentation, so exam preparation never becomes a scramble.
Coordinate responses to regulator, auditor, and partner-bank inquiries with Compliance, Legal, and Operations.

Lead Goal tracking, and Reporting for Fraud & Disputes

Own the cadence and content of Operational Quality Reviews and Monthly CORs Reviews for Fraud and Disputes, from the data pull to the narrative to the follow-up actions.
Define and track ops health measures and team goals, including OKRs, so leaders can see what is on track, what is at risk, and why.
Build the reporting and dashboards leaders use to make decisions, and set up new reporting from scratch where none exists.
Raise risks early, make trade-offs explicit, and drive decisions to closure with partners who don't report to you.

Use data for continuous improvement

Analyze quality, productivity, and compliance data across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX to find the patterns behind recurring problems.
Turn those findings into durable process, tooling, and reporting improvements instead of one-off fixes.
Work with QC, L&D, and Operations leaders to route root causes to the team that can fix them, and confirm the fix worked.
Stand up new continuous improvement programs from zero to one and measure their results.

What You'll Bring:

5+ years of program management experience in risk, compliance, fraud, disputes, or operations at a bank, fintech, or other regulated financial services company.
Banking* experience, with working knowledge of how a regulated institution runs, and direct experience working with regulators, examiners, auditors, or sponsor banks (for example exam preparation, findings remediation, or regulatory responses).
A record of building programs from zero to one, from ambiguous problem to measurable result, with impact beyond your immediate team.
2+ years of experience governing BPO or other outsourced operations, with a focus on governance: SLAs, performance and quality oversight, escalations, and regular business reviews.
Strong understanding of risk operational processes in Fraud and/or Disputes, such as case handling, investigations, chargebacks, or Reg E error resolution.
Comfort with data: you can define metrics, build or interpret dashboards, and explain what the numbers mean.
Experience using AI and automation to improve how work gets done, for example synthesizing evidence and documentation, drafting and maintaining SOPs, analyzing QC and vendor data, summarizing incidents, and automating status reporting.

Nice to Haves:

Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or above) or equivalent continuous improvement experience
ISO quality credentials (for example ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Implementer) or a similar quality management background
PMI certification (PMP, PgMP) or equivalent
Experience with change management frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR, or ITIL-style incident and problem management

Job Description

Air & Space Force Solutions (ASFS) is a Business Area within the Intelligence & Security division of the Platform & Services segment of BAE Systems Inc. ASFS is responsible for the execution of all Air & Space Force-related programs within I&S and for business operations and growth in this market. The Air & Space Force Solutions Business Operations manager will report directly to the VP/GM and will be a member of the ASFS senior leadership team. The Business Operations Manager directs all areas of business operations, both on a daily basis as routine issues arise, executing a wide and challenging range of support activities that underpin the efficient operations of this large and complex business, and looking to the future as they undertake the planning and execution of longer-term strategic operations and initiatives. The individual in this role will actively participate in all business reviews and decisions and manage all reporting requirements upwards. They delegate tasks and responsibilities to appropriate personnel, identifying and resolving issues and conflicts within the business unit. They interpret companywide policies and processes and establish ASFS operating policies and processes that ensure the smooth operation of the business. They interact frequently with all levels of the business and with external management/stakeholders. We offer flexibility for the hire to work from our McLean, VA, Hill Air Force Base, Forth Worth or Fort Walton Beach office.

Specific responsibilities of this position will include but not be limited to:

Enterprise Rhythm-of-Business Orchestration: Design and enforce a unified cadence for MBRs/QBRs/MMRs—including pre-read standards, KPI thresholds, and corrective action tracking—ensuring upstream executive alignment and downstream execution.

Integrated Program Governance: Serve as the conduit between VP/GM and ASFS Leadership Team; consolidate program status, risks, and dependencies across multiple factory locations to drive cross-functional decision-making.

Board-Ready Analytics & Storytelling: Prepare executive-level reporting that synthesizes operational performance, cost/schedule outcomes, and mission-critical improvement initiatives into clear narratives and scenario-based recommendations.

Coordinating MBRs, QBRs, data call responses for ASFS, liaison with Functions, MMRs, monitor and tracking of training.

Planning and Management of ASFS facilities, including facilities rationalization, improvements and new requirements.

Program Resource Management at Scale: Lead cost estimation, allocation, tracking, and deep-dive variance analysis across a portfolio of programs; tie resource decisions to contractual baselines and operational capacity.

Forecasting & Executive Presentation: Prepare and present comprehensive forecasts—including sensitivity analysis to senior leadership and internal/external customers; translate complex trends into actionable financial levers.

Networked Facility Strategy: Direct facility rationalization and growth planning across sites; develop business cases for improvements and new requirements that optimize safety, capacity, and mission readiness.

Safety Program Leadership: Oversee proactive safety initiatives (e.g., hazard assessment, preventive maintenance, readiness reviews) aligned with corporate standards; track leading indicators to reduce risk.

Audit Program Ownership: Lead internal/external audits end-to-end—scoping, readiness, execution, and remediation—while strengthening control environments that pass inspection repeatedly.

Operational Rigor Frameworks: Establish and enforce incident management, change management, and release governance standards to ensure stability and high availability of platforms and services.

Capability & Training Portfolio: Monitor, report, and improve employee training across safety, compliance, and technical domains; tie certification pathways to operational roles and mission-critical readiness.

Culture of Accountability & Learning: Promote a high-performance culture through transparent metrics, root-cause analysis, and shared lessons learned; recognize teams for measurable improvements.

Community Investment & Sponsorships: Manage sponsorships and community investment planning aligned to ASFS priorities; track impact and employee engagement outcomes.

Integration & Realignment Leadership: Lead complex integration efforts (org design, process harmonization, systems consolidation) and realignment initiatives that enhance efficiency and reduce handoffs.

Predictive Analytics & Early Warning: Lead initiatives that use predictive models to flag capacity constraints, defect trends, and incident precursors; activate preventive actions to avoid customer impact.

Operational Readiness & Capacity Planning: Set capacity, staffing, and tooling strategies for peak-load scenarios; validate readiness through simulations and after-action reviews.

Coordinating MBRs, QBRs, data call responses for ASFS, liaison with Functions, MMRs, monitor and tracking of training

KPI Suite & Dashboards: Develop and track key operational metrics (availability, incident response, MTTR, throughput, customer impact, cost/schedule performance); publish role-based dashboards for transparency.

Variance & Trend Analysis: Perform recurring variance analyses across cost, schedule, and quality; drive root-cause containment and monitor the efficacy of corrective actions over time.
