jobs.description:
Overview

The AFGHS project is funded by the U.S. Department of State (DoS) to support the delivery of lifesaving, comprehensive maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) and malaria services across Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar. It aims to improve service and data quality, strengthen health-system integration and resilience, facilitate effective transition, and promote local ownership and accountability for sustained health outcomes.

Jhpiego works closely with the Ministries of Health in Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, the Reproductive and Child Health Section (RCHS), the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP), the Zanzibar Malaria Elimination Programme (ZAMEP), and Regional Administration and Local Government (RALG) structures to align implementation with national priorities and strengthen locally led implementation and oversight.

Position Summary

The Senior Program Manager (SPM) provides leadership and oversight for implementation of the AFGHS-Jhpiego project across Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, directing and coordinating field implementation across MNCH and malaria components. The SPM ensures that approved workplan activities, milestones, and implementation priorities are translated into coordinated regional and council-level action and delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with government priorities, Jhpiego requirements, and Department of State expectations.

Reporting to the Sr Project Director and working closely with the Project Management Team, Technical Directors, MEL team, and Field Team Leaders, the SPM leads day-to-day implementation planning, coordination, performance management, and problem-solving. As the custodian of the project workplan, the SPM monitors progress against approved milestones and payment-linked deliverables
, identifies implementation gaps and risks, and coordinates corrective actions to support timely achievement, verification, and payment of milestones.

The SPM plays a central role in ensuring that implementation is government-led and designed for sustainability and transition from the outset. The SPM works with Field Team Leaders and government counterparts to integrate project-supported activities within national, regional, and council plans, budgets, systems, and routine service delivery; strengthen subnational capacity and accountability; and progressively shift appropriate implementation, management, monitoring, and quality improvement functions to government and local structures while maintaining continuity and quality of essential services.

This position will be closed on October 15, 2026.

Responsibilities

Field Implementation Management and Integration

Lead implementation management and coordination of field execution across project-supported regions.
Translate approved work plan into integrated implementation schedules, deployment plans, and execution timelines.
Ensure field teams work closely with RHMTs and CHMTs to coordinate field implementation, align project activities with regional and council priorities and work plans, and strengthen government leadership, ownership, and oversight of implementation.
Support coordination with other DoS implementing partners and relevant stakeholders at regional and council levels to promote complementarity, integration, efficient use of resources, and avoidance of duplication.
Facilitate joint planning, implementation reviews, and problem-solving with government counterparts, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to address implementation gaps and bottlenecks and maintain progress toward agreed results.
Ensure alignment of field activities across project-supported regions to optimize efficiency and coverage.
Monitor implementation progress and identify delays, gaps, or risks, escalating issues to the Sr Director and Technical Directors with analysis and options.

Supervision and Performance Management

Provide direct operational and administrative supervision to Field Team Leaders and the Senior Program Officer.
Set clear performance expectations and ensure accountability for field and functional execution.
Support Field Team Leaders in supervising staff and enforcing approved schedules and standards.
Foster a culture of execution discipline, teamwork, and problem-solving.

Implementation Planning and Readiness

Coordinate field readiness for planned activities, including staffing, logistics, transport, approvals, and sequencing.
Work closely with the Senior Program Officer to align logistics plans with deployment schedules.
Identify and address implementation dependencies in advance, adjusting sequencing within approved plans and escalating technical changes as required.

Subgrantee Design and Oversight

Support the design of project subgrants, including scopes of work, deliverables, milestones, and performance expectations, in collaboration with technical, MEL, grants, and finance teams.
Provide programmatic oversight of subgrantees to ensure timely, high-quality implementation aligned with project objectives, work plans, and government priorities.
Monitor subgrantee performance against agreed deliverables and milestones, identify implementation gaps, and coordinate corrective actions as needed.
Ensure subgrantee activities are integrated with field implementation and coordinated with government, DoS implementing partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

Monitoring, Data Use, and Follow-Up

Oversee tracking of implementation progress toward project milestones and deliverables, using project data and relevant national routine reporting and surveillance systems.
Use programmatic data and field reports to identify gaps or risks to milestone achievement, coordinate corrective actions, and document adaptations and lessons learned.
Provide regular updates to project leadership on progress toward milestones, highlighting implementation bottlenecks, risks, and actions required to ensure timely achievement and verification.
Government and Partner Coordination
Lead operational engagement and coordination with RALG structures at national, regional, and council levels, and with relevant implementing partners and stakeholders.
Ensure field implementation is aligned with government priorities, work plans, calendars, administrative processes, coordination mechanisms, and milestone timelines.
Facilitate joint implementation planning, performance reviews, and problem-solving with government counterparts and partners to address bottlenecks and maintain progress toward agreed results.
Represent the project in relevant implementation and coordination forums, as delegated, and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions.

Compliance, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

Ensure field implementation complies with Jhpiego policies, Department of State requirements, national guidelines, and approved project procedures.
Contribute to development and review of project work plans, budgets, reports, and performance reviews, ensuring field implementation is accurately reflected.
Ensure timely and complete field documentation and reporting to support accountability, milestone verification, and audit readiness.
Promote continuous improvement through routine performance review, adaptive management, and timely follow-up on identified gaps and corrective actions.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health, Public Administration, Project Management, Social Sciences, or a related field required.
Professional certification in Project Management (e.g., PMD Pro, PMP) is an advantage.
9-10 years of experience overseeing multi-region field implementation or project management of large-scale health programs.
Demonstrated experience working with Ministry of Health, national programs, RHMTs and CHMTs donor-funded implementing partners, and engaging private sector and faith-based organizations.
Experience supporting donor-funded health programs, preferably U.S. Government-funded projects.
Proven experience supervising decentralized field teams and coordinating complex implementation schedules.
Familiarity with national health management information and logistics systems and digital learning platforms including DHIS2, eIDSR, UCS, MSDQI, eLMIS, and ECHO.
Strong coordination, management, and communication skills.
Fluency in Kiswahili and English required.
Willingness to travel up to 40% across Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar.
Experience conducting supportive supervision, on-the-job mentorship, and capacity building for health workers and community cadres, including CHWs and iCCM providers.
Experience working with government health structures at regional, council, facility, and community levels, including RHMTs and council health teams.
Demonstrated ability to support routine data collection, review, and use for performance monitoring and service improvement.
Experience using or adapting supervision tools, checklists, job aids, and basic technical reporting formats.
Familiarity with U.S. Government-funded health programs is an advantage.

Preferred Qualifications

Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external customers those contacted during work.
Planning and negotiation skills required
Good level of computer literacy, conversant with all Microsoft products

As part of the continued development of its North American operations, the company is strengthening its automation capabilities in Mexico to support increasingly complex projects and progressively build stronger local project execution capabilities.

To support this new phase of growth, the company is looking to recruit an Automation Project Manager
, who will play a central role in managing robotic automation projects.

The position is based in Querétaro
, primarily on-site, with travel required depending on project needs.

Missions

Reporting directly to the Head of Operations for North America and acting as the main coordination point for automation projects in Mexico, you will be responsible for keeping projects under control from purchase order through installation, customer acceptance, and final project closure.

Your role will combine Project Management, technical coordination, customer management and process development, connecting customers, sales, suppliers, engineering, service, management, and international teams.

You will support the gradual transition from a highly outsourced automation execution model toward a more balanced approach combining the capabilities of international teams with stronger local project execution capabilities in Mexico.

End-to-End Automation Project Management

You will manage automation and robotics projects from start to finish, from purchase order through engineering, manufacturing, testing, installation, commissioning, customer acceptance, and final project closure.
You will develop, maintain, and monitor project schedules, clearly communicating project status and potential deviations to customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
You will continuously monitor project scope, budget, costs, margins, schedule, and technical execution, identifying changes or deviations that could affect successful project delivery.

International Coordination and Customer Management

You will help develop repeatable project templates, checklists, meeting formats, installation plans, customer communication standards, and project tracking tools.

Profile

You hold a degree in Engineering, Automation, Mechatronics, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics, Industrial Engineering, or another relevant technical field.
You bring at least 5 years of professional experience in industrial project management, ideally managing automation, robotics, machinery, capital equipment, manufacturing equipment, or other complex technical projects.

You demonstrate strong project ownership and accountability, taking responsibility for project progress and ensuring that commitments are followed through.
You are proactive and solution-oriented, with the ability to anticipate problems and coordinate multiple stakeholders to drive solutions.
You have a strong customer-focused mindset, both internally and externally, and know how to build trust through professional, timely, and accurate communication.
You have an advanced level of English, both written and spoken.

Why Join Our Client?

This position offers the opportunity to join an established international industrial group and global leader in robotic automation.

You will have significant autonomy and international exposure, working directly with industrial customers, technical teams and management on projects where your ability to maintain control, anticipate risks, communicate clearly, and drive solutions will have a direct impact on project performance and customer satisfaction.

Expérience en préparation opérationnelle, en mise en service, en démarrage d’usine ou en opérations industrielles.
Excellentes compétences en coordination de projets, en planification, en résolution de problèmes et en organisation.
Capacité à collaborer avec des équipes multidisciplinaires et à gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément.
Maîtrise des outils de gestion de projet, de production de rapports et d’analyse de données.
Disponibilité pour effectuer des déplacements et travailler sur les sites des clients, selon les besoins.

jobs.title: Cyber Data Analyst
jobs.description:
This is a Fully Remote Job

About Our Client:

The organization operates within the cybersecurity sector, focusing on vulnerability management to enhance security program effectiveness. It addresses challenges related to data integrity and program performance measurement by transforming raw scan, asset, and remediation data into reliable metrics. This enables leadership and stakeholders to understand risk posture accurately and supports informed decision-making.

About the Opportunity:

The CYBER DATA ANALYST is responsible for managing the analytics, reporting, and data quality aspects of a vulnerability management program. This role involves developing trusted metrics and dashboards, utilizing AI-assisted tools to identify and correct data defects, and collaborating with operational teams to improve data processes. The position is impactful in shaping how the security program measures and reports on its performance and risks.

Responsibilities:

Manage monthly data-quality reporting to identify and track data-integrity issues.
Design and refine AI-assisted workflows for large-scale data defect detection and correction.
Maintain version-controlled libraries of prompts, scripts, and workflows for reproducibility.
Reconcile business intelligence reports with authoritative vulnerability scan data.
Verify and certify vulnerability and asset ownership through coordination with operational teams.
Develop new reports, metrics, scoring algorithms, and dashboards based on stakeholder needs.
Transition mature analytics products to operational teams with documentation and training.
Collaborate with operations to trace data defects to root causes and recommend process improvements.
Produce audit-ready documentation for regulatory and stakeholder review.
Support additional analytical, reporting, and program improvement initiatives as assigned.

Requirements:

Minimum of 1 year experience in data analysis, data science, business intelligence, security analytics, IT operations reporting, or related fields.
Ability to work with large and imperfect data sets, including data joining and reconciliation.
Proficiency in building reports and dashboards with data modeling and calculated measures.
Advanced Excel skills, including lookups, pivot tables, and conditional logic.
Experience leveraging AI tools for analytical and data remediation tasks with sound judgment.
Familiarity with cybersecurity concepts such as vulnerabilities, patching, CVEs, CVSS scoring, and risk fundamentals.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical and leadership audiences.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and SharePoint.
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks within deadlines.

$55,271 - $62,808 per year, depending on experience and qualifications.

Join a financial services firm where your contributions are valued. Edward Jones is a Fortune 500¹ company where people come first. With over 9 million clients and 20,000 financial advisors across the U.S. and Canada, we’re proud to be privately-owned, placing the focus on our clients rather than shareholder returns.

Behind everything we do is our purpose: We partner for positive impact to improve the lives of our clients and colleagues, and together, better our communities and society. Are you passionate about turning data into meaningful business outcomes? We are seeking a collaborative and analytical Business Analyst I to support strategic initiatives across our Service Division. In this role, you will leverage data, business insights, and operational expertise to help drive decision-making, improve processes, and deliver solutions that enhance the client and advisor experience.

As a key partner to business leaders, operations teams, and technology stakeholders, you will transform complex data into actionable insights, lead and support cross-functional initiatives, and represent Service Division priorities in enterprise-wide programs. This role offers a unique opportunity to combine business intelligence, project coordination, process improvement, and stakeholder engagement while developing expertise in core service functions, including Cash & Banking, Transfers & Rollovers, and Estates.

The ideal candidate is naturally curious, highly organized, and excels at connecting data, people, and processes to solve business challenges and drive continuous improvement.

What You'll Do

Transform complex data into actionable insights by creating reports, dashboards, and visualizations that support strategic and operational decision-making.
Partner with business leaders to gather requirements, analyze business needs, and translate them into meaningful reporting and analytical solutions.
Lead or support cross-functional initiatives, coordinating timelines, priorities, risks, and deliverables to ensure successful execution and measurable business outcomes.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls, and operational efficiency, while quantifying and communicating the potential business impact of recommended changes.
Use Jira and other workflow tools to document requirements, manage work items, track progress, and provide visibility into project status and dependencies.
Build strong relationships across business, operations, and technology teams, facilitating discussions that drive alignment, accountability, and results.
Develop expertise in Service Division functions, including Cash & Banking, Transfers & Rollovers, and Estates, to effectively support business priorities and initiatives.
Represent Service Division needs in enterprise programs and value stream initiatives, ensuring solutions align with operational goals and deliver an exceptional service experience.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Analytics, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
2+ years of experience in business analysis, business intelligence, operations, project coordination, or a related analytical role.
Experience gathering business requirements, analyzing data, and developing insights and recommendations to support business decisions.
Advanced Excel skills and experience with reporting and visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence platforms.
Experience using Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar tools to manage work, document requirements, and track project progress.
Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and collaborate across teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting cross-functional projects, process improvement initiatives, or business transformation efforts.
Financial services, wealth management, banking, or service operations experience.
Experience influencing stakeholders and driving outcomes without direct authority.
Knowledge of service-related functions such as Cash & Banking, Transfers & Rollovers, Estates, or similar operational areas.
Experience documenting business processes and identifying opportunities to improve operational efficiency.

Candidates that live within a commutable distance from our Tempe, AZ and St. Louis, MO home office locations are expected to work in the office four days per week.

jobs.title: Cyber Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

The role of Cyber Security Analyst
is important to us.

As part of our dedicated Cyber Security team, you will report to our Head of Cyber and be based from our offices in Crewe, Cheshire.

As a Cyber Security Analyst, you will play a key role in protecting systems, networks, and data against cyber threats. You will participate in threat detection and incident response efforts, support the development of security policies and controls, and work closely with stakeholders to ensure compliance and security best practice across the business.

You will also assist with maintaining and improving the company’s accredited Information Security Management System (ISMS), with a particular focus on ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials Plus requirements.

In addition, you will work collaboratively with the wider Cyber Security team to define and mature Security Operations Centre (SOC) processes, ensuring the effective day-to-day operations of security controls.

This is an excellent opportunity for a seasoned professional to contribute to a high-performing Cyber Team in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

Your Responsibilities Day To Day Will Be…

Work closely with IT Operations teams and wider business functions to implement and optimise technologies and security controls that enhance the organisation's cyber security posture across internal and customer-facing platforms.
Proactively identify cyber security risks, control deficiencies and opportunities for security improvement, making recommendations to reduce organisational risk.
Support the design, implementation and ongoing development of cloud-based infrastructure and services, ensuring security best practices are embedded by design.
Collaborate with software development teams to ensure secure design principles and cyber security requirements are integrated throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC).
Create, maintain and review cyber security policies, standards, procedures and technical documentation.
Monitor security events and alerts, conducting threat detection, investigation and incident response activities to minimise business impact.
Perform vulnerability management activities, including vulnerability identification, risk assessment, remediation tracking and reporting.
Conduct threat intelligence research, analysing emerging threats, vulnerabilities and attack techniques, and recommend appropriate security improvements.
Work with third-party security vendors, managed service providers and consultants to support security operations, resolve issues and implement security enhancements.
Lead cyber security projects and initiatives aimed at improving the organisation's security capability, resilience and compliance posture.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of security monitoring, detection and response capabilities across the organisation.
Assist with security risk assessments, audits, compliance activities, and the implementation of security controls aligned to recognised frameworks and standards.

What do we expect of you?

Technical Knowledge And Skills

Strong technical knowledge of cyber security and its practical application across technology environments.
Good understanding of application security and experience working with development teams to promote secure development practices.
Experience with Vulnerability Management, penetration testing and security assessments, including prioritising and driving remediation.
Experience with EDR, NDR and SIEM technologies, including security monitoring, alert investigation and response.
Understanding of cyber incident response, including triage, investigation, containment and recovery.
Knowledge of Cyber Essentials, Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO 27001.
Good understanding of operating systems, infrastructure and networking, including Windows and Linux environments, servers, virtualisation, databases, web servers, TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls and common infrastructure security controls.
Good understanding of cloud security, preferably AWS, including IAM, logging, monitoring and configuration.
Understanding of DLP, data security and open-source/software supply-chain risk.
Good understanding of network security, WAFs, IAM and secure architecture principles.
Understanding of Red Teaming, Continuous Adversarial Testing and Vulnerability Disclosure Programmes.
Understanding of Cyber Threat Intelligence, phishing, social engineering and insider risk management.
Good understanding of MITRE ATT&CK and NIST Cybersecurity Frameworks.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate technical security issues and recommend appropriate actions.
Ability to produce clear technical documentation, reports and security recommendations.
Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Understanding of ITIL/service management principles and the ability to manage and prioritise multiple activities.
Commitment to keeping up to date with emerging technologies, threats and cyber security practices.

Behavioural Expectations

Works with autonomy and drive - takes initiative, identifies what needs to be done and proactively progresses work through to a successful outcome.

jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

The Fraud Strategy Data Analyst provides enterprise-level analytical insight into fraud decisioning performance, fraud risk reduction, customer experience, operational efficiency, and financial outcomes across deposits, digital, payments, authentication, and the end-to-end account lifecycle. Through advanced, data-driven analysis, this role evaluates alert performance, decision accuracy, queue dynamics, loss drivers, customer friction points, operational inefficiencies, and emerging fraud risks to identify opportunities that improve fraud outcomes and business performance.

By developing and applying consistent fraud tradeoff, loss avoidance, and decisioning performance frameworks, the analyst translates complex analytics into actionable, decision-ready insights that enable leadership to optimize fraud controls, improve detection effectiveness, reduce customer friction, enhance workload management, and prioritize investments based on measurable enterprise impact. The role does not design or implement fraud rules or strategies but provides the analytical foundation that informs enhancements to fraud decisioning, mitigation processes, and enterprise fraud initiatives through close partnership with Fraud Strategy, Risk, Operations, Digital, Technology, and AI/ML teams.

Key Responsibilities:

Leverage advanced technical proficiency in SAS/SQL/Python, and related analytical tools to extract, transform, and analyze large-scale fraud data, delivering scalable, data-driven insights that support fraud decisioning, tradeoff analysis, performance measurement, and strategic business decision-making.
Analyze enterprise fraud performance across deposits, digital, payments, authentication, and account lifecycle domains to identify material loss drivers, customer friction, operational impacts, emerging risks, and opportunities to improve fraud outcomes.
Evaluate fraud decisioning performance, alert effectiveness, decision outcomes, false positive rates, workflow execution, and queue dynamics to identify performance gaps, inefficiencies, and optimization opportunities.
Assess end-to-end fraud operations, including alert lifecycle performance, queue throughput, review capacity, case-handling efficiency, and workload distribution to improve operational effectiveness and scalability.
Develop and apply fraud tradeoff, loss avoidance, and performance measurement frameworks that quantify the impact of fraud controls across fraud loss reduction, customer experience, operational efficiency, and financial outcomes.
Engineer, maintain, and enhance methodologies for measuring fraud benefit, losses avoided, operational costs, customer friction, false positives, and overall business impact using transparent, audit-ready approaches.
Conduct advanced and ad hoc analytics, root-cause investigations, and performance assessments to evaluate fraud controls, identify emerging threats, uncover inefficiencies, and support optimization or decommissioning decisions.
Monitor fraud trends, alert behavior, decision outcomes, and operational performance to identify emerging risks, changing fraud patterns, anomalies, and degradation in control effectiveness.
Quantify expected benefits, costs, risks, operational impacts, and tradeoffs associated with fraud initiatives, tools, models, and strategic enhancements to support investment prioritization and business case development.
Partner with Fraud Strategy, Fraud Mitigation Solutions (FMS), Risk, Operations, Digital, Technology, and AI/ML teams to align priorities, evaluate performance, validate findings, and drive measurable fraud and business outcomes.
Support predictive fraud, AI, and analytics initiatives through performance assessment, value measurement, operational impact analysis, and ongoing benefit tracking.
Develop and maintain performance metrics, dashboards, reporting frameworks, and executive-level insights that provide transparent visibility into fraud outcomes, decisioning effectiveness, operational efficiency, and business impact.
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable, and executive-ready recommendations that inform strategy, investment decisions, operational improvements, and continuous enhancement efforts.
Ensure analytical rigor, data integrity, and methodological consistency by validating assumptions, strengthening measurement frameworks, and delivering decision-ready insights that can be confidently used by leadership and governance forums.

Additional Expectations

Leverage approved AI‑enabled productivity tools to improve efficiency, quality, and effectiveness of work outputs, applying sound judgment to validate results and ensure responsible, compliant use in accordance with company policies.
Develops and delivers data‑driven insights and narratives to inform decision‑making and support business objectives.
Perform additional duties and assume evolving responsibilities as needed to support changing business priorities, organizational needs, and strategic objectives.
Maintain a strong commitment to regulatory compliance, internal controls, and risk management standards by adhering to applicable laws, policies, and procedures. Comprehensive knowledge of all departmental data sources, and of fraud risk and operations management associated with the product lines

Proficient computer navigation skills using a variety of software packages including Microsoft Office applications and data analysis software

jobs.description:
About the Team:

Mercury* is building a complete financial stack for startups, and Risk is how we protect our customers, Mercury, and the broader financial ecosystem. You'll join the Fraud & Disputes Enablement team, a shared-services group that makes our operations teams faster, more consistent, and ready for scrutiny. The team is made up of Quality Control, Learning & Development, and Program Management, and supports Fraud & Disputes.

Role Summary:

This is a generalist program management role for someone who builds programs from zero to one. You'll lead Mercury's Bank Charter Readiness work across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX, run the operating reviews and goal tracking that show leaders how Fraud and Disputes are performing, and use data to drive continuous improvement. You'll work with Risk Operations, Compliance, Risk Product, Engineering, Risk Strategy, and Vendor Management, and you'll show the team how AI can help us work smarter, not harder.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What You'll Do:

Lead Bank Charter Readiness

Translate the regulatory expectations of a chartered bank (Reg E, card network rules, and the standards examiners apply) into clear, sequenced work plans owned by the right teams.
Build Bank Charter Readiness programs from zero to one: define scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks, and report progress to executives.
Keep teams audit-ready every day, with current SOPs, traceable decisions, defensible evidence, and clean documentation, so exam preparation never becomes a scramble.
Coordinate responses to regulator, auditor, and partner-bank inquiries with Compliance, Legal, and Operations.

Lead Goal tracking, and Reporting for Fraud & Disputes

Own the cadence and content of Operational Quality Reviews and Monthly CORs Reviews for Fraud and Disputes, from the data pull to the narrative to the follow-up actions.
Define and track ops health measures and team goals, including OKRs, so leaders can see what is on track, what is at risk, and why.
Build the reporting and dashboards leaders use to make decisions, and set up new reporting from scratch where none exists.
Raise risks early, make trade-offs explicit, and drive decisions to closure with partners who don't report to you.

Use data for continuous improvement

Analyze quality, productivity, and compliance data across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX to find the patterns behind recurring problems.
Turn those findings into durable process, tooling, and reporting improvements instead of one-off fixes.
Work with QC, L&D, and Operations leaders to route root causes to the team that can fix them, and confirm the fix worked.
Stand up new continuous improvement programs from zero to one and measure their results.

What You'll Bring:

5+ years of program management experience in risk, compliance, fraud, disputes, or operations at a bank, fintech, or other regulated financial services company.
Banking* experience, with working knowledge of how a regulated institution runs, and direct experience working with regulators, examiners, auditors, or sponsor banks (for example exam preparation, findings remediation, or regulatory responses).
A record of building programs from zero to one, from ambiguous problem to measurable result, with impact beyond your immediate team.
2+ years of experience governing BPO or other outsourced operations, with a focus on governance: SLAs, performance and quality oversight, escalations, and regular business reviews.
Strong understanding of risk operational processes in Fraud and/or Disputes, such as case handling, investigations, chargebacks, or Reg E error resolution.
Comfort with data: you can define metrics, build or interpret dashboards, and explain what the numbers mean.
Experience using AI and automation to improve how work gets done, for example synthesizing evidence and documentation, drafting and maintaining SOPs, analyzing QC and vendor data, summarizing incidents, and automating status reporting.

Nice to Haves:

Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or above) or equivalent continuous improvement experience
ISO quality credentials (for example ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Implementer) or a similar quality management background
PMI certification (PMP, PgMP) or equivalent
Experience with change management frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR, or ITIL-style incident and problem management
Experience in QC program design, workforce management, or learning and development
Familiarity with card network dispute rules and platforms
Experience with Risk UX, customer-facing risk flows, in a regulated context
Experience building and scaling a program in a high-growth environment

All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. Provides executive-level reporting, dashboards, and health assessments to support informed decision-making, governance, and strategic prioritization. Ensures programs remain aligned with organizational goals while balancing scope, schedule, financial, risk, and resource considerations.

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Strong skills and experience in issue resolution, influencing team members and other stakeholders, conducting difficult negotiations and managing to stringent timelines for project deliverables
Demonstrated superior understanding of business and technology organization, resources, priorities, needs and policies
Demonstrated leadership in the implementation of complex programs and projects

Demonstrated executive level verbal and written communication skills
Superior working knowledge of business matters, finance, planning, and forecasting

In-depth knowledge of management and planning systems theory and practical application to complex initiatives
Experience with financial measurements and metrics
Financial Services experience

Experience implementing large/complex initiatives across a matrix organization.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Company Description

Trupanion is a leading provider of medical insurance for cats and dogs in North America. Our mission is to help loving, responsible pet owners budget and care for their pets. At Trupanion, we offer a collaborative, casual, and pet-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to be themselves.

Job Description

The Technology Program Manager is responsible for the successful delivery of complex technology programs consisting of multiple related projects and workstreams. Working closely with business partners, project managers, vendors, and technology functions, this individual provides program-level leadership, governance, integrated planning, and coordination to ensure projects collectively achieve program and organizational objectives.

This position is open to candidates in the Seattle, WA area. You will have a hybrid remote/in-office schedule where you will work from our casual, pet-friendly office at least 3 days a week.

Responsibilities

Lead corporate-wide IT programs consisting of multiple related projects and workstreams.
Define program objectives, scope, priorities, roadmaps, governance, milestones, and success measures.
Create and maintain integrated and interlocking schedules across projects and track cross-project dependencies.
Understand how individual projects affect the program and exercise judgment in elevating issues and risks to the appropriate level.
Coordinate project managers, business stakeholders, vendors, contractors, and technology resources to support effective program execution.
Establish program-level risk, issue, dependency, decision, and change-management practices and drive resolution of cross-project blockers.
Provide leadership and mentoring to project team managers, foster a positive team environment, and provide direction in ambiguous situations.
Use negotiation, influence, and creativity to resolve conflicts involving scope, schedule, costs/budget, risks, dependencies, and resources across the program.
Establish program status reporting and provide consolidated visibility into milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and overall program health.
Coordinate third-party vendor activities and monitor vendor performance across program workstreams.
Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure proper organizational change readiness

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, Management Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent work experience.
6+ years of project/program management experience in a professional technology environment, including responsibility for complex cross-functional initiatives.
Hands-on experience with SDLC and implementation methodologies, including Agile and Waterfall.
Proficiency with PMO collaboration tools such as Planview, Microsoft Project, or Portfolio for Jira.
PMP, PgMP, Scrum, SAFe or similar certification preferred

Skills

The successful candidate will possess business operations experience and skills, analytical and critical thinking skills, and attention to detail. Additionally, the ideal candidate should possess the following:

Drive effective teamwork, communication, collaboration, and commitment across multiple disparate groups with competing priorities
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and ability to flex communication style with technical and non-technical users
Comfortable exercising judgment and using analytical skills in ambiguous situations
Ability to work well with people from many different disciplines with varying degrees of technical experience.
Organizational, prioritization, and time management skills
Ability to work with minimal supervision
Strong collaborative skills with an ability to effectively communicate with both technical teams and non-technical business users/leaders
Ability to learn quickly and adapt to a changing environment; proactive in seeking out information when necessary
Passion for and a desire to delight the customer
Creative problem solving, organization, attention to detail, flexibility, and adaptability are crucial to the success of this role.
Experience monitoring and managing vendor performance

Compensation

The base salary range for this position is $115,000 - $125,000 USD on a full-time schedule.
Along with base salary, Trupanion employees may be eligible for monthly bonuses.
We want all employees to be invested in Trupanion’s success, so we grant Restricted Stock Units to all new team members. Our new hire grants vest over 4 years.

Additional Information

Benefits and Perks:

Full medical, dental, and vision benefits at no cost to the employee
Four weeks of paid time off and 9 paid float holidays (you can decide which days are most important to you!)
Five-week sabbatical after five years of employment
Open, casual, pet-friendly, and fun office environment
Free medical health insurance for your pet (1 dog or cat)
Paid time off to volunteer at nonprofit organizations
Seattle Office Amenities: Free on-site gym, free dog walking services for office pets during business hours, free parking, and paid ORCA cards.

For more information about Trupanion, visit https://trupanion.com/about

Learn more about how Trupanion has revolutionized our industry and the reimbursement model: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vdWZ4KHiPTQ

Trupanion is an equal-opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, abilities, perspectives, and skills.

We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodations.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

jobs.title: Sr. Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own.

We’re actively seeking a talented Sr. Operations Analyst to join our team in Omaha, NE or Newport Beach, CA.

The Senior Operations Analyst serves as a strategic partner to business leaders by owning the Quality Control framework for back office operations and delivering actionable insights through advanced data analysis and reporting. This role combines QC oversight, business analysis, and data analytics to ensure operational service delivery is performed in line with expectations, SLAs, and regulatory requirements — while also supporting decision-making, improving operational efficiency, and driving cost reduction across the organization. Sitting within the business/Operations team, the position serves as the bridge between Operations and Technology, translating business and QC needs into clear reporting requirements without owning system build or development. The role plays a critical part in driving operational health, mitigating risk, and enhancing reporting capabilities that align with business objectives.

How You’ll Help Move Us Forward

Reporting Responsibilities

Researches, collects, analyzes, models, and reports on data used to support decisions on day-to-day operations and to assess business and performance issues with a focus on quality, productivity, efficiency, and cost reduction.
Researches internal and external best practices and QC benchmarks to establish standards for use in evaluating operations.
Supports reporting across the operating model, with the ability to deliver platform-specific and integrated views — including QC dashboards, SLA performance, and error trend reporting.
Understands end-to-end business drivers, including valuation and pricing, and partners with Pricing/Actuarial teams to ensure reporting and analysis reflect core business economics.
Serves as the bridge between Operations and Technology, collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders (Operations, Technology, Finance, Compliance) to translate business and QC needs into clear reporting requirements — without owning build, development, or system configuration.
Researches, collects, and analyzes operational and performance data to identify trends, variances, and opportunities.
Identifies and recommends enhancements to reporting techniques, and analytical tools to drive operational health, and hands off well-scoped requirements to Technology for execution.
Identifies and fills operational reporting gaps by working directly with Operations leaders on high-impact process areas.

Quality Control (QC) Responsibilities

Champions the QC program based on strategy set by Operations Leader, including call QC, transactional QC, and process QC across in-house and outsourced (TPA/BPO) delivery channels, with sampling methodology, scorecards, and calibration protocols.
Ensures accountability across stakeholder groups and confirms service is performed in line with SOPs, contractual obligations, and regulatory expectations, flagging deviations, control gaps, and re-work trends through targeted and random sample reviews of transactions (e.g., overpayments, enhanced death processing, annuity certificates, disbursements).
In partnership with Operations Leadership, drive corrective action plans (CAPs) and coaching feedback loops, converting QC findings into SOP updates, training opportunities, and process refinements.
Maintain an audit-ready trail of QC reviews, findings, and resolutions to support internal audit, compliance, and external regulatory reviews.

The Experience You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
5+ years of combined experience in operations quality control/business analysis, and/or data analytics, preferably within financial services, insurance, or annuity back office operations, and visualization using tools such as PowerBI, Qlik or Tableau.
Demonstrated experience championing the QC program with oversight and partnership from key stake holders (call QC, transactional QC, or process QC).

What Makes You Stand Out

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex data and QC findings into actionable insights.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to deliver findings to senior leadership and influence corrective action.
Ability to work independently with limited guidance.
Familiarity with predictive modeling, statistical analysis, and business intelligence best practices.
Working knowledge of actuarial or pricing methodologies, either through prior actuarial/pricing roles or close partnership with actuarial teams in a business or analytics capacity is a plus.

Base Pay Range

The base pay range noted represents the company’s good faith minimum and maximum range for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered to a candidate will be dependent upon several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications and geographic location. Also, most employees are eligible for additional incentive pay.

$89,010.00 - $108,790.00

Your Benefits Start Day 1

Your wellbeing is important to Pacific Life, and we’re committed to providing you with flexible benefits that you can tailor to meet your needs. Whether you are focusing on your physical, financial, emotional, or social wellbeing, we’ve got you covered.

Prioritization of your health and well-being including Medical, Dental, Vision, and Wellbeing Reimbursement Account that can be used on yourself or your eligible dependents
Generous paid time off options including: Paid Time Off, Holiday Schedules, and Financial Planning Time Off
Paid Parental Leave as well as an Adoption Assistance Program
Competitive 401k savings plan with company match and an additional contribution regardless of participation

You Can Be Who You Are

We are committed to a culture of diversity and inclusion that embraces the authenticity of all employees, partners and communities. We support all employees to thrive and achieve their fullest potential.

What’s life like at Pacific Life? Visit Instagram.com/lifeatpacificlife

To request an accommodation, contact a Human Resources Representative at Pacific Life Insurance Company.

jobs.title: KYC Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
The KYC Operations Analyst is responsible for participating in Anti-Money Laundering (AML) monitoring, governance, oversight and regulatory reporting activities in coordination with the Compliance and Control team. The overall objective of this role is to assist in the development and management of a dedicated internal KYC (Know Your Client) program at Citi.

Responsibilities:

Partner with Relationship Management and Compliance teams to assist with the preparation, development, due diligence and approval of the electronic Know Your Client (KYC) record and supporting appendices
Validate the information within KYC records and Customer Identification Program (CIP) documents to ensure completion and accuracy
Ensure KYC records incorporate local regulatory requirements / Global Business Support Unit (BSU) Standards
Assist Citi on KYC efforts in accordance to the NAM Retail AML KYC Ops (NTB) procedures
Perform KYC reviews (Scheduled & Unscheduled Reviews for Individual Client types across varied risk classes) including monitoring and tracking of KYC records, assisting with the development and execution of action plan for expiring records, and ensuring records are not past due
Determining if the accounts are in scope
Client Identification, Verification and Screening
Information such as customer’s address, employment (including employer), connectivity to PEP/SPF (Sanctions Screening), will be validated and confirmed. These will be validated based on existing information available or through approved third party sites. Based on the results, enhanced due diligence checks will be performed which include negative news and social media checks
Partner with internal units to ensure adequate due diligence process is carried out for customer accounts and documentation reviews
Ensure all information and documentation comply with local regulation and Citi standards
Send the requests to Outreach/RM for accounts where information is required to complete the review
Any suspicious product usage from AML perspective gets highlighted to senior management for further reviews promptly
Ensure to maintain quality standards (90% and above) for the KYC reviews undertaken
Ensure any tech issue/procedural clarifications gets highlighted to managers for further review and guidance
Ensure to get Quality Control (QC) review done on files prior to submission and respond/correct any discrepancies identified during QC reviews
Submit record for Business Approval once review is complete and respond/correct any discrepancies identified during BA reviews
Willing to work in night shifts

A sense of urgency with strong attention to detail and high degree of accuracy

Ownership mentality and the discipline to run a recurring daily control process without prompting

jobs.description:
Introduction to the job

Do you aspire to a position where your data-driven insights help shape business decisions at one of the world’s leading high-tech companies? At ASML, the Business Intelligence & Analytics (BI&A) team creates value from data by generating insights and industrializing analytical solutions across sectors and business lines. This helps prioritize business initiatives and to initiate change. Our work supports decision-making on topics ranging from operational excellence and business performance to customer support, manufacturing, supply chain, service operations, and revenue optimization.

As a business analyst at ASML it is your role to collect, analyze and translate our data into business insights. You will support the generation of business insights by using a combination of cross-sector data sources and applying leading analytics tools and technologies on these sources in order to enable optimization of ASML and customer value.

Role and responsibilities

As a Business Analyst, you will work on a diverse portfolio of projects that contribute to ASML’s business priorities across multiple domains and functions. You will:

Generate business insights by translating data into meaningful visuals, reports and dashboards and recommendations.
Support the formulation of problem statements and perform exploratory data analysis to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities.
Apply leading analytics tools and technologies to develop in-depth understanding of structured and unstructured data on the topic at hand.
Collaborate with technical and non-technical (cross-sector) stakeholders across sectors to understand business challenges and translate them into analytical solutions.
Present analytical approaches, results, and recommendations in a clear and compelling manner to drive informed decision-making.
Contribute to improving business performance through data-driven insights that create measurable value for ASML and its customers.

Education and experience

We are looking for high-potential Business Analysts who are eager to learn, challenge themselves, and grow within a dynamic environment. Drive, curiosity, and learning agility are at least as important as prior experience.

A technical master's degree (or you will graduate in the upcoming months), preferably within a strong technical direction like Mathematics, Physics, Data Science, Mechanical or Electrical/Industrial Engineering or Econometrics.
Experience with data analysis methodologies, tools and techniques.
Ability to apply modern analytical and statistical approaches to complex business problems.
Experience with tools such as Python, Databricks, Power BI, Spotfire and/or Alteryx.
Business sensitivity and ability to make the step from theoretical models to creating business impact

Skills

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

To thrive in this job as business analyst, you bring:

Strong capability for problem solving.
Perseverance to ‘find the needle in the haystack’.
Able to work effective and constructive in multidisciplinary teams.
Strong communication and presentation skills, enabling you to explain analytical concepts to various audiences.
A structured and accurate way of working with a focus on quality and efficiency.
Pragmatic, pro-active, ‘self-propelling’ way of working and able to operate in a dynamic environment.
Take responsibility: 'say what you do and do what you say'.
Customer focus and the ability to anticipate stakeholder needs.
The ability to connect data, business context, and strategic objectives.

Distributed Analytics Network

This job position is part of the Distributed Analytics Network (DAN), a network consisting of analytics entities (called Analytics Nodes) throughout the different sectors at ASML. The main objective of DAN is to create an aligned way of working across the organization and elevate ASML's analytics capabilities to the next level. Being part of DAN provides exposure to multiple teams, business domains, and stakeholders across ASML, creating unique opportunities for learning, development, and career growth.

Other Information

If this job description sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you. Please upload your resume and a brief motivation explaining why you are interested in joining ASML and how you can contribute as a Business Analyst.
An online assessment and in-person business case assessment are part of the recruitment process.

This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the United States Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R.

730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require ASML to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.

Inclusion and diversity

ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. jobs.description:
Profound is the fastest-growing AI marketing platform, used by 15% of the Fortune 500 including Comcast, Estée Lauder, and Walmart, and innovators like Ramp, MongoDB, and Figma. It is where marketing teams do the work: research, briefs, content, campaigns, reporting, all in one place, alongside agents that carry the load with them.

Built on 2B+ real user prompts and growing, Profound’s data shows you what people ask AI and what the models say back. Profound's AI Marketer joins that data with deep context about our customers to find the opportunities worth acting on, and then puts agents to work: automating reporting, drafting content, auditing pages for readability, running competitive research. It measures what works and gets better every day.

As GTM Enablement Program Manager, you'll help to build and shape Profound’s most high-impact programs and initiatives across our GTM functions. Partnering with the GTM leaders and cross-functional teams, you'll own the construction, execution and iteration of the enablement programs end-to-end. You'll build systems and run them, which includes cross-functional program leadership, direct training and enablement of tenured reps, along with content and curriculum development for managers, reps, and new hires. You’ll work closely with these teams to identify gaps and opportunities for improvement in performance and effectiveness both during and beyond ramp. This role will function as an individual contributor alongside our Field Enablement team to execute and measure against performance indicators both at the individual and business level. You will have the creativity and space to design programs that leave a lasting impact across the business at large.

What you'll do

Own enablement programs end to end, from scoping and needs analysis through build, rollout, measurement, and iteration.
Partner with GTM leaders across Sales, CS, Marketing, Product, and RevOps to turn business priorities into clear program goals, owners, and timelines.
Build and deliver content and curriculum for new hires, tenured reps, and managers, including outlines, decks, playbooks, and role plays.
Facilitate live trainings and workshops for audiences ranging from new hires to senior leaders.
Up-level front-line and second-line leaders as they build their teams, with a focus on coaching, inspection, and reinforcing new behaviors in the field.
Identify performance gaps during and beyond ramp, and design targeted programs to close them.
Define success metrics for every program and track them at both the rep and business level, reporting results to stakeholders.
Lead the implementation and adoption of enablement technology as we build out that arm of the function.
Work alongside the Field Enablement team to keep programs consistent, well documented, and easy to scale.

Who you are

9+ years of combined experience in client-facing roles and revenue enablement, including 4+ years in a direct client-facing role (Sales or Customer Success) and 5+ years on a Revenue Enablement Team.
You’ve built and run programs end to end in B2B SaaS and can point to measurable business results.
You influence senior stakeholders with professionalism and respect while holding your ground when priorities compete.
You are a strong facilitator and communicator, comfortable leading a room of new hires one day and a leadership team the next.
You have coached or enabled front-line managers and know how to turn manager behavior into rep behavior.
You have rolled out enablement tools and driven real adoption, not just implementation.
Meticulous in your ownership: your content, plans, and follow-through are accurate and on time.
A self-starter and team player with high energy who works well with autonomy and ambiguity.
Curious and experienced with AI; you work to implement and leverage it to change both the way we sell and the way we support our GTM teams.

Location

This is an on-site role based in our NYC office, designed for builders who thrive on speed, iteration, and meaningful impact.

For this role, the expected base salary range is $180,000 to $220,000. Profound’s total compensation package is designed to be competitive and includes base salary, equity, and a full range of benefits and perks. new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Administers all finance, human resources and facilities and other operational activities for small to mid-sized academic or research program. Administers major program components, and some or all of the program's operational requirements. Develops and organizes conferences and other public forums. Works under direction of Principal Investigator or more senior Academic Program Officer to establish center agenda, funding, objectives.

The Molecular Oncology Initiative (MOI) at UCSF is responsible for enabling precision oncology for cancer patients at UCSF, driving both the clinical implementation of personalized cancer care and the research that advances it.

MOI provides support for clinicians in the interpretation of our own internal tumor sequencing platform (UCSF500) as well as platforms offered by external vendors.

The MOI Program Manager will play a central role in this mission, operating under the direction of the MOI Director and Associate Director as well as supervision by HDFCCC administration.

The MOI Program Manager will lead the MOI Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC), reviewing and quality controlling the work and providing constructive, actionable feedback to support accuracy and continuous improvement in data collection and abstraction activities.

The MOI Program Manager will be expected to work with considerable independence alongside MOI team members to execute MOI activities, taking ownership of implementation while operating within a framework of regular oversight and guidance .

The current job responsibilities for this position do not involve any direct patient contact. Candidates must live or plan to move to the Bay Area and are required to come to Mission Bay campus at least twice and preferably three times a week.

This Position Has Two Core Areas Of Responsibility

Program Management — serving as the operational backbone for MOI's clinical and research activities, shepherding projects from inception to completion
Data Quality Management — taking a leading role in designing, testing, and implementing automated pipelines for the collection and quality assurance of clinical and genomic data across all MOI projects, while also performing manual QC as required to ensure data integrity across all activities.This includes also design and data management using RedCap and other database tools.

Department Overview

The UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center (HDFCCC) is redefining what is possible by advancing cancer research and patient care. By unifying outstanding researchers and clinicians, the center minimizes cancer incidence, establishes new frontiers in cancer care, and improves our patients’ lives. We have received the prestigious designation of “comprehensive” from the National Cancer Institute (NCI).We combine basic science, clinical research, epidemiology, cancer control and patient care throughout the University of California, San Francisco.

The Molecular Oncology Initiative (MOI) at UCSF is responsible for enabling precision oncology for cancer patients at UCSF, driving both the clinical implementation of personalized cancer care and the research that advances it. MOI provides support for clinicians in the interpretation of our own internal tumor sequencing platform (UCSF500) as well as platforms offered by external vendors.

Qualifications

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training required including but not limited to biological sciences, biomedical informatics, public health, or a related discipline.
Minimum of 3 years of experience in program management, data quality control, or a related role, preferably in an academic medical or research setting
Strong foundational knowledge of medical terminology and clinical oncology concepts, including cancer diagnoses, staging, pathology, imaging, and treatment modalities (e.g. surgical, systemic, and radiation therapies); this knowledge is essential for independently and accurately performing quality control of clinical oncology data abstractions
Demonstrated experience with IRB submissions, contract management, or other research compliance and oversight activities
Experience performing clinical data abstraction and/or quality control of clinical or genomic data
Familiarity with electronic health records (EHR) and the ability to navigate complex patient clinical histories spanning diagnoses, imaging, pathology, and treatment records
Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, maintain document control systems, and track and follow up on action items across a team to ensure project/task completion in a timely manner.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear meeting notes, program updates, and reports for diverse audiences
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively, with a demonstrated capacity to proactively identify problems and develop solutions with minimal supervision
Proficiency with standard project management tools.
Prior experience with various computer programs (Microsoft Office; internet-based databases).
Ability to sit and work at a computer for several hours per day. May need to travel between one or more campuses via UCSF shuttle.
Ability to work with a sensitive population of patients (oncology patients).
Ability to work well independently, complete projects in a timely manner, and prioritize multiple projects to ensure the completion of essential tasks by deadlines.
Excellent problem-solving skills and able to use good judgement in application of problem-solving skills.
Effective at applying constructive feedback on projects and performance.
Thorough knowledge of administrative, budgetary, human resources and financial principles and practices.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Strong ability to think creatively and independently on concepts requiring advanced analytical skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work with diverse groups to achieve results.
Strong ability to work collaboratively with internal and external peers and managers.

Preferred

Terminal degree in a related area (PhD, JD, MD, etc.) such as biological sciences, biomedical informatics, computational biology, public health, or oncology-related discipline and / or equivalent experience / training.
3–4 years of experience in program management and/or data quality control, ideally within a precision medicine, oncology, or genomics program
Familiarity with cancer genomics and next-generation sequencing (NGS), including experience interpreting or working with NGS test results such as the UCSF500 panel
Experience with oncology-specific data standards and ontologies, including OncoTree or similar cancer classification systems
Experience with REDCap database design, build, and maintenance
Experience designing or implementing automated data abstraction or QC pipelines
Practical experience working with large language models (LLMs) and the ability to thoughtfully evaluate when LLM-based solutions are appropriate versus rule-based or heuristic approaches
Experience providing feedback, guidance, or informal mentorship to junior research staff or coordinators
Familiarity with UCSF systems and institutional policies, including UCSF research compliance frameworks
Solid fundraising experience.
Academic background and experience in selected area of research preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training required including but not limited to biological sciences, biomedical informatics, public health, or a related discipline.

About Us

About UCSF

The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is a leading university dedicated to promoting health worldwide through advanced biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care. It is the only campus in the 10-campus UC system dedicated exclusively to the health sciences. We bring together the world’s leading experts in nearly every area of health. We are home to five Nobel laureates who have advanced the understanding of cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, aging and stem cells.

A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

U.S. Bank’s Digital Assets and Emerging Money Movement team is seeking an effective Senior Program/Project Manager
with demonstrated program leadership and project management experience to contribute to the success of our enterprise money movement initiatives. This role sits within a new and evolving team focused on enterprise‑level money movement strategy.

This individual will lead and direct large, complex programs in support of the bank’s overall money movement strategy. The role provides direction to project staff across multiple workstreams and stages within assigned programs, establishes program governance, and drives execution to ensure initiatives are implemented, adopted, and operating effectively. The Senior Program/Project Manager translates corporate objectives into clear program objectives, operating practices, and measurable outcomes.

The Emerging Money Movement team operates with an enterprise‑first mandate
and is not aligned to a single business line. While individual business lines retain ownership of their own product roadmaps and growth strategies, this team focuses on cross‑line‑of‑business coordination, optimization, and reuse of money movement capabilities to reduce duplication and drive enterprise‑wide efficiency.

The team is evolving from a historical focus on external advocacy and industry engagement toward a model centered on internal enterprise program leadership and strategic coordination.
